authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan sources, focusing on underetymologised and smaller sources first for greater diversity. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have unlimited time now

proposals.evidence: Dhakal p. 48 prints /bʰəike/ “to become” beside a separately negated form. Turner9416 gives Pali bhavati, Prakrit bhavaï, Ḍoḍi bhōṇō and other regional verbs “become”; Darai -ike is the regular infinitive, and its bhəi- stem matches the Middle Indo-Aryan bhavai family.

proposals.evidence: Dhakal p. 54 prints /dziuno/ “living.” Turner5244 is the living participial family, with Kumaoni jyūno, Nepali jiũdo and Kotgarhi j̈iundɔ “living, alive.” These adjective comparanda select 5244 rather than noun jīva “life” (5239) or verbal jīvati (5241).

proposals.evidence: Dhakal p. 56 prints /dzəri/ “root.” Turner5086 section 1 lists Nepali jari, Bihari jar, Maithili jaṛi and Oriya jaṛa with the same meaning. This identifies the regional root family, while Turner leaves its remoter Dravidian versus Munda history unsettled.

proposals.evidence: Dhakal pp. 65 and 69 print /adzu/ “today.” Turner242 specifically lists Prakrit ajja, Apabhraṃśa ajju, Sindhi aju and Nepali āju, matching the Darai voiced affricate and final u. This is the adyá branch, not adyāpi “even now” (243).
